inspiration: A homing ball chases its target at a speed that depends on distance: at 50 m or closer it adds a small offset to the target's max speed, at 250 m or farther it adds a larger one, and linear in between. The change of speed is limited to a 5-second slew, so a sudden shortcut does not make the ball jump (src/items/rubber_ball.cpp 304-307, 560-585). The data sets the near offset to 9.0 and the code clamps it to at least 10.0 after loading (data/powerup.xml line 78; src/items/rubber_ball.cpp 355-356). That is a real mismatch to note, not to copy.

Drops are chosen by finishing position: each rank has its own weight row, one random number is taken modulo the summed weights and walked cumulatively to pick the item (src/items/powerup_manager.cpp 415-448, 609; data/powerup.xml 101-120). The back of the pack gets a different table, which is catch-up without a visible rubber band.

Explosive drops are swapped for a harmless one for the first 15 seconds of a race (data/stk_config.xml 239; src/items/powerup_manager.cpp 623-624). It is an opening grace rule, cheap to copy as a zone field.

Difficulty is a row of multipliers on the base kart: easy takes 0.6 of max speed, medium 0.8, hard 0.92, and the best row is left unchanged (data/kart_characteristics.xml 348-361). A small stat-modifier table that a fast duel can use.

The data files accept relative values such as multiply by a factor or add then multiply, evaluated left to right with no operator precedence (data/kart_characteristics.xml comment lines 1-22). Useful as a rule for catalogue fields, with the precedence trap written down.

A particle burst is data: a sphere emitter with a wide spread, a high emission rate for a short life, a size that grows over time, and a single white colour range (data/gfx/explosion.xml 2-29). A good catalogue shape for VFX (row 8), with the numbers in data.
Each item kind has its own glow colour set in one table (data/items.xml). A visible rarity or type code at a glance, set as data rather than in code.

Kart size classes are light, medium and heavy, with width, height and length per kart in one list (data/official_karts.xml). A ready shape for a hero or creature size table that keeps silhouettes readable at 375 px.

briefs.label: Homing bouncer with distance-scaled speed
briefs.why: A projectile that speeds up when far and eases off when close reads as a clear threat. The slow change keeps it honest when the target moves round a corner.
briefs.keep: speed depends on distance to the target; the change is slew-limited so it cannot jump; a bounce arc gives it a visible path
briefs.change: our projectile is a chain of glyphs, not a ball; the speed band is 0.8x to 1.3x of the target's walk speed; the slew takes 2 seconds, not 5
briefs.ref: src/items/rubber_ball.cpp 552-598 (updateWeightedSpeed), data/powerup.xml 75-86 (item block). Recreate as an original projectile; do not copy the code or the item name.

briefs.label: Finishing-position drop table
briefs.why: Every place has its own drop weights, so the back of the pack gets better odds without a visible catch-up rule.
briefs.keep: one weight row per rank; one random number taken modulo the summed weights; cumulative walk to the pick
briefs.change: the row is chosen by loss streak in a zone, not by rank; the drops are our own item set with no names from the donor; the weights are zone data
briefs.ref: src/items/powerup_manager.cpp 415-448 (getRandomItem), 609; data/powerup.xml 101-120 (weight docs). Recreate as an original drop table.

briefs.label: Opening grace on explosive drops
briefs.why: New arrivals in a zone are not hit by big bursts for the first few seconds, so the first minute is fair.
briefs.keep: a timed rule swaps the explosive pick for a harmless one until the timer passes; the timer is data
briefs.change: for us, the first 10 seconds of a zone visit swap to a stagger, shown as a grey tell so the player sees the swap
briefs.ref: data/stk_config.xml 239 (timeout value); src/items/powerup_manager.cpp 623-624 (swap). Recreate as an original zone rule.

briefs.label: Difficulty as a multiplier table
briefs.why: One base kart and a short list of multipliers gives easy, medium and hard without copies of the stats.
briefs.keep: difficulty rows multiply the base; the top row is the base itself; fields are named once
briefs.change: express the multipliers as zone fields with a clamp; name the rows by the zone's threat level, not easy/medium/hard; add a per-row hit-point multiplier
briefs.ref: data/kart_characteristics.xml 348-361. Recreate as an original difficulty table.

briefs.label: Sphere burst that grows
briefs.why: A burst that spreads and grows reads as an impact at a glance, even at 375 px wide.
briefs.keep: sphere emitter, wide spread, high rate for a short life, a size that grows over the life
briefs.change: a flat ring of sparks in our palette instead of a sphere; life of 0.4 seconds to fit the hit-stop; no white, use our own colour range
briefs.ref: data/gfx/explosion.xml 2-29. Recreate as an original hit burst.
